pr_title: Create a new page for "Add new profile" in the SUI
pr_body:
- Whenever we add a new profile setting from now on we have to update
  `Profile::CopySettings` _and_ `CascadiaSettings::DuplicateProfile` 👎 

Notes from bug bash (checked bugs have been resolved):

- [ ] The duplicate list can be very long if you have profiles
- [x] DH: "Create new" seems too vague. "New empty profile" or something
  seems a little clearer to me.
- [x] There is no deduplication counter for name
- [x] Crash when your settings file is corrupt and we had to fall back
  to the defaults and you duplicate a profile
- [x] Crash due to #10003

## PR Checklist
* [x] Closes #9121

issue_context.title: "Add a profile" should lead to its own page
issue_context.body:
# Description of the new feature/enhancement

Currently, adding a profile in the Settings UI is a bit simplistic: click "add new" and you're taken to a new profile. "Add new" should be expanded to be its own page that can include the following:
- create a new profile (standard)
- duplicate a profile
- (after #3818) create a profile based on another one
- import a profile (via JSON?)

[Click here for a rough design.](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/blob/main/doc/specs/%231564%20-%20Settings%20UI/cascading-settings.md#add-new----duplicate-profile)

review_comments: const doesn't do meaningful things for winrt types.

Is there some way we could add a test for this? To maybe prevent us from forgetting this in the future? 

Maybe like if we did something where we:
* duplicate a profile ("A" -> "A Copy")
* manually change the name of "A Copy" back to "A"
* Call `ToJson` on both profiles and compare the results?

Just to clarify - what would be the purpose of this test? If we want to check whether duplicating is working as intended, we could just compare the profile objects themselves without calling `ToJson` right?

I'm not sure that a Profile actually implements any sort of logical compare with other profiles - so I was thinking the ToJson would be a handy shortcut, rather writing code that actually compares the values of each and every property.

This is more of a thought experiment so you can ignore it for now

if you add a profile and then go BACK to this page, does it contain the new profile?

if you change a profile name and go back to this page, does it show the new name?

1. Yes
2. Yes (as long as the textbox lost focus at some point before you switched back to the add profile page)
nit: a quick sentence on how this differs from `Profile::Copy` might be helpful here

Just so we're clear: when you duplicate Command Prompt, what do you get? When you duplicate WSL, what do you get? When you have a `defaults` layer, and then duplicate a leaf profile, what do you get?

I think that Command Prompt will give you a full JSON block. I think that WSL will give you a partial JSON block. I think that having a `defaults` layer will _copy all of the defaults into the new json block_.
This does not seem right to me?
Solved the `defaults` layer issue by adding a `UserDefaults` origin tag and checking for it!

Curious: were these changes necessary? I figured defining them outside of the for-loop would save a bit of time, but I did that because I honestly don't know how expensive doing `try_as` twice for each `item` was.

If I recall (Pankaj can clear this up), we were treating the selected item _DIRECTLY_ as a string, or as a PVM, every time we hit a string or PVM in the Items list. This meant that when we were iterating over a *profile*, we would attempt to access `->Guid()` on the selected item (oops).
That is: we automatically treated the selected item _as a profile_ if we happened to be iterating over a profile. That would _of course_ explode when the selected item was not a profile.
Bonus points: add a test that specifically covers the dynamic profile case (since that one is more complex)
